title: Firebase Auth, account membership, invites, and MCP OAuth

surfaces.currentBehavior: Firebase Auth supplies email/password and Google identities and persistent sessions. Membership documents supply account, role, and financial-access authorization; no active custom-claim authorization was found. Public HTTP Functions verify Firebase bearer tokens. MCP exchanges Firebase identity for its own HMAC OAuth tokens.

surfaces.currentBehavior: Observes Firebase auth state; signs in/up with email/password, signs in with Google credential exchange, and signs out only from Firebase Auth.

surfaces.currentBehavior: Reads/subscribes account roots directly, calls createAccountHttp with a Firebase bearer token, and exposes a direct account update that production Firestore rules deny.
surfaces.notes: Target account mutations must use an authorized command rather than a possibly dead direct-write path. M2 map reviewed under target-mapping-method.md; target authority is capability-specific and contains no Firebase application adapter.

securityRequirements: Account bootstrap/update and membership changes require verified Principal and capability, validate resulting owner/admin/financial state and record server actor/time
syncRequirements: Authorized Account/membership/default-reference results enter bootstrap/admin streams through one durable operation result; clients never write role fields directly

migration.rule: Map source Accounts/members/default definitions to stable target IDs and typed bootstrap/admin operations; preserve source correlation and report denied/orphan/duplicate/default variants.
reconciliation: Account, owner membership, member grants and seeded default IDs/counts/hashes reconcile atomically per source Account

tests: Account bootstrap idempotency/atomicity, owner/admin/financial validation, cross-account denial, default seeding and migration tests
acceptance: An Account is created or administered once through trusted operations and cannot be partially bootstrapped or client-edit its authorization

surfaces.currentBehavior: Subscribes to account members, discovers all user memberships with a cache-first users collection-group query, and lets admins update role and financial-access fields.
surfaces.notes: Target must make multi-account discovery deterministic and enforce member update permissions server-side/RLS. M2 map reviewed under target-mapping-method.md; target authority is capability-specific and contains no Firebase application adapter.

securityRequirements: One verified issuer/subject resolves to a stable Principal; active Account membership and server-owned role/financial grants authorize every request
Account discovery is non-enumerating and no caller-selected UID, Account fallback or service credential substitutes for Principal authority
syncRequirements: Bootstrap streams contain only authorized Account summaries and the caller's membership/capability snapshot; Auth subjects and secrets are not synchronized

migration.rule: Correlate Firebase Auth identities and membership paths to stable Principals/auth identities/account memberships, preserve provider/source IDs for audit and quarantine ambiguous or duplicate identity links.
reconciliation: Every source identity/membership maps once with issuer/subject/Principal/Account/role/financial grants or an explicit blocking quarantine

tests: Identity correlation, Account discovery, cross-account/revoked/expired/non-enumerating access, membership grant and app/MCP parity tests
acceptance: The same Principal/membership authority governs app and MCP without exposing provider IDs or inferring an Account

surfaces.currentBehavior: Subscribes to unrevoked/unaccepted invites, creates UUID-token invite documents directly, and revokes by timestamping the invite.
surfaces.notes: Current backend rules allow any account member, not only admins, to write invites. M2 map reviewed under target-mapping-method.md; target authority is capability-specific and contains no Firebase application adapter.

securityRequirements: Invite secrets are opaque, one-time, expiring and stored only as digests; preview is rate-limited/non-enumerating and accept binds authenticated Principal/email under capability checks
syncRequirements: Only authorized admin invite summaries synchronize; raw secrets/digests/Auth subjects do not. Preview/accept are online typed queries/operations with durable results

migration.rule: Map source invite lifecycle/proposed grants to stable invite IDs and one-way token digests, preserve source audit/correlation and reject expired/revoked/accepted/duplicate variants deterministically.
reconciliation: Every source invite maps to one lifecycle state and proposed-access hash or quarantine; accepted invites reconcile to exactly one Principal membership

tests: Secret digest/no-enumeration/rate-limit/expiry/revoke/one-time accept/email binding/cross-account and migration tests
acceptance: An invite reveals only approved preview fields and grants membership exactly once after authenticated acceptance

surfaces.currentBehavior: Builds and parses custom-scheme and Firebase Hosting invite URLs, previews invites through a public HTTP endpoint, and accepts them with a Firebase ID-token bearer request.
surfaces.notes: User-visible invite URL compatibility may require a redirect/transition period at cutover. M2 map reviewed under target-mapping-method.md; target authority is capability-specific and contains no Firebase application adapter.

target.owner: External Entry Points and Invite Routing
securityRequirements: Only allowlisted HTTPS hosts/routes and validated bounded payloads are accepted; a link never grants membership or contains backend secrets
syncRequirements: Link parsing produces a typed local intent; invite preview/accept then use current authenticated online contracts and normal membership Sync

migration.rule: Map supported source custom/Firebase-hosting URLs to stable provider-independent product routes during the compatibility window; record unsupported/environment-mismatched links explicitly.
reconciliation: Route inventory maps each source/target link form to one typed intent, environment, deprecation outcome and test fixture

tests: Host/scheme allowlist, environment isolation, malformed/oversized payload, no-authority link and legacy-route compatibility tests
acceptance: Changing Auth/hosting does not break product links or let a URL bypass authenticated invite acceptance
